title: AI-assisted solo development in Godot: Crimson Ark gameplay, with a free Steam demo
author: GneulGames
selftext:
I'm developing Crimson Ark solo in Godot, using AI for artwork and coding assistance. It's a single-player dark fantasy RPG with loot hunting, equipment upgrades, and auto-hunting.



One practical lesson has been that an effect looking good in isolation doesn't mean it works in combat. Players can equip eight skills, so I've been revising effects for consistency and readability, and checking performance when attacks hit groups of enemies.



Watching other people play also showed me things I'd stopped noticing as the developer: some didn't realize they could learn skills from different branches early on. I've been revising the tutorial around that.



This is a 33-second excerpt from an actual play session. There's a free Windows demo on Steam if you'd like to try it: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5317790/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5317790/)



There are no microtransactions or paid summon currency; summon resources come from gameplay.



For other developers using AI assets, how do you keep visual consistency once several effects are on screen? I'd also welcome impressions from anyone who tries the demo.
